tagline: Across the Sea Islands to a lighthouse built to move
intro: East of Beaufort, US 21 connects Saint Helena Island with Harbor Island and Hunting Island, crossing a landscape of tidal marsh and barrier islands. South Carolina designated the corridor a scenic highway in 1979. The state transportation department emphasizes expansive views and Hunting Island State Park at the route’s end. There, maritime forest fills the interior, with saltwater marsh on the western side and more than four miles of beach.

Bridges connected the outer Sea Islands with Beaufort in the 1930s, while the Civilian Conservation Corps developed Hunting Island as a state park. The US 21 designation reached Hunting Island in 1953. The highway once continued to the island’s south end, but erosion destroyed part of it about 1980. The state made a new park entrance and one-lane roads through the palmetto forest. At Harbor River, a fixed bridge replaced the narrow 1939 swing span in 2021, changing the crossing used to reach the outer islands.

From Beaufort, the island journey passes through Saint Helena, a center of Gullah culture and language. Continue to Harbor Island, where US 21 provides the only vehicle access, then to Hunting Island between Harbor and Fripp islands. US 21 ends where it once turned east toward the lighthouse.

moments.title: Saint Helena Island
moments.text: Saint Helena is an inland Sea Island, surrounded by marshes rather than fronting the Atlantic. It is a major center of Gullah culture and language. At Penn Center, that cultural work shares a site with the history of education after emancipation. Penn School was founded in 1862 for formerly enslaved people and moved to its present site in 1864. Darrah Hall at Penn Center is part of Reconstruction Era National Historical Park. Nearby, The Green continues to host community meetings, celebrations and gatherings. The Green occupies the site of the first Darrah Hall, destroyed in 1893.

moments.title: Harbor Island
moments.text: Most of Harbor Island is tidal marsh, and US 21 is its only road connection. The highway through it was constructed in the 1930s to link Saint Helena and Hunting islands. A swing bridge built in 1939 carried traffic over the Harbor River. Narrow and structurally deficient, it was replaced by a fixed span that opened on April 25, 2021. The island also supports a volunteer sea-turtle nest protection program permitted by the South Carolina Department of Natural Resources. Development remained limited until The Fripp Company bought most of the island and created a gated residential and resort community.

moments.title: Hunting Island State Park
moments.text: Hunting Island’s lighthouse was built to come apart. Its cast-iron shell consists of bolted sections, with a brick lining carrying the main structural load. Completed in 1875, this tower replaced an earlier lighthouse destroyed during the Civil War. The movable design proved necessary: severe beach erosion threatened the station, and in 1889 the lighthouse, keeper’s house and two other structures moved a mile to their present location. The cast-iron sections weigh up to 1,200 pounds each, bolted together to make a shell that could be dismantled. The tower’s upper third is black; the lower two-thirds are white.
moments.notice: The lighthouse has a cast-iron outer shell and a black upper third above its white lower section.
